title: MedChemBench is a test on old papers. It is not a new drug.
friendlyTitle: This chemistry test uses old papers. It is not a new drug.
summary: On 20 November, OpenAI introduced MedChemBench, 99 problems drawn from published medicinal-chemistry papers. At the xhigh setting, OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra earned 84.5 percent of the available credit, against 58.2 percent for GPT-5.6 Sol. Selecting compounds and predicting numbers scored lower than rebuilding a molecule's structure.
friendlySummary: On 20 November, OpenAI introduced MedChemBench. It is 99 problems taken from published papers about designing drug molecules. At its highest reasoning setting, OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra scored 84.5 percent of the available points. GPT-5.6 Sol scored 58.2 percent. Choosing the next molecule, and predicting measured numbers, scored worse than rebuilding the molecule's structure.
whyItMatters: OpenAI says the scores do not show that a model can discover a drug or improve a lab decision. The papers may already have been in training, and each answer was one attempt, with no tools and no new experiment. A score on a published paper is not a result from your bench.
